ï»¿# CareCircle

**Care together, closer always.**

CareCircle is a family-care coordination application for the IS216 Group Project, Section G8. Families can share tasks, maintain care profiles and notes, follow appointment journeys, and recognise the people lending a hand.

One person can belong to multiple families. Each family has its own recipients, tasks, updates and Contributions leaderboard. **My tasks** brings together the signed-in person's claimed tasks across their families.

This README describes the implementation in this repository. External integrations require configuration; the limitations below distinguish working features from placeholders.

## Project resources

| Resource | Link |
| --- | --- |
| Hosted frontend | [CareCircle on Vercel](https://care-circle-delta-one.vercel.app/) |
| Task allocation and progress | [Team tracker](https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1q4JjWnC077RomNEm6pJjR2DpeRkb-RZyNa4O9ssRjLk/edit?gid=77767454#gid=77767454) |
| Wireframes | [Figma designs](https://www.figma.com/design/oo8lDXmN1OIF7zJ75SPn3a/Preline-UI-Figma--Community-?node-id=299804-16564&t=bZtps8beujV1iiui-1) |
| Proposal, specifications and database design | [Team document](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1C0RIz2fLhAb1berm-wca4x8c-Li_FNyRMWFHNJV37T8/edit?tab=t.0) |
| Project update presentation | [13 October slides](https://www.canva.com/design/DAHXlRxCktA/P5yOdcJa_RUiOY1k8l6CRQ/edit) |

## Features

### Accounts, families and preferences

- Register, sign in and sign out with hashed passwords and JWT authentication. Signing out revokes the existing session token.
- Create a family, join using an invitation code, and switch between multiple families. Invitation codes contain 10 hexadecimal characters and can be regenerated by an admin.
- Manage members and admin/member roles, remove members, or leave a family. The last admin cannot be removed or demoted.
- Edit your name, phone, Telegram username, language preference and profile picture. Email is read-only in the profile form.
- View another member's profile and recent tasks from shared families. Profiles are accessible to the account owner and people who share a family with them.
- Choose light, dark or device appearance, saved in the browser and applied across pages and dialogs.
- Save an English, Chinese, Malay or Tamil preference. Care-log translation is requested separately; this does not automatically translate the entire interface.

### Family home

- See the greeting, care recipients, today's tasks, active transit banners and recent updates in one dashboard.
- Browse recipients using numbered pages, three cards per page. Cards show upcoming care and tasks needing someone, and open the recipient hub.
- Browse tasks inside Home using **Today**, **Needs someone**, **Overdue**, **Claimed**, **In progress**, **Completed** and **All tasks**. There is no separate Family tasks page.
- Claim available tasks from Home. Expired unclaimed tasks move out of Needs someone and into Overdue automatically.
- Scroll the task panel and Recent updates independently while their headings remain visible.
- Follow multiple active trips, with additional trips behind an expandable control.
- Open profiles from identified account/recipient photos on desktop and mobile. Linked recipients open their account profile; recipients without accounts open their care profile.
- Receive task changes through polling and a shared query cache. Recent updates uses the family's notification history, with local session updates as a fallback.
- Use responsive mobile navigation and family switching. Users without a family see create/join options.

### Care recipients

- Create and edit profiles for elderly care, pregnancy, postpartum care, infants, injuries and other care needs.
- Record names/nicknames, profile pictures, birth dates, mobility, allergies, conditions, dietary restrictions, medications, emergency contacts, preferred clinic and care notes.
- Use the recipient hub's **Overview**, **Tasks**, **Log** and **Profile** tabs. Overview combines upcoming tasks, latest notes and essential care information.
- Link a recipient to your own account within a family. Infant profiles cannot be linked to accounts.
- Opt into **I'm also a care recipient** in My Profile. Saving creates or reactivates one linked recipient per family; the setting also applies when creating or joining another family.
- Toggle that setting repeatedly without creating a new recipient ID each time. Opting out hides the linked profiles while preserving tasks and care history.
- Archive recipients instead of deleting them. The record and account link remain available for historical tasks/logs and later reactivation.

### Tasks and shared responsibilities

- Create tasks for a recipient or the household with title, description, category, start/end time, location and optional transport requirement.
- Categories: appointment, therapy, errand, groceries, childcare, medication, companionship and other.
- Search Singapore locations through OneMap and save the address, postal code and coordinates.
- Claim from Home, recipient task lists or task details. The server assigns the signed-in member rather than accepting a client-supplied assignee.
- Unclaim a task before starting it, returning it to the family. Either the claimer or task creator can release the claim.
- Prevent double claims with a conditional database update: simultaneous requests have one winner; the other receives a conflict.
- Close claiming at the scheduled start time. Both the UI and database write condition enforce the deadline. An overdue task can be unclaimed, but cannot be reclaimed unless its schedule changes.
- Start and complete claimed tasks. Starting a transport task creates a real transit session.
- View task details, status, location, assignment and timestamp-based activity. Creator-only edit/delete APIs and creator/admin cancellation APIs enforce lifecycle restrictions.
- Make confirmed task edits through the assistant. Repeating tasks also have an Edit dialog with occurrence/series scope; the conventional Edit button for ordinary tasks remains a placeholder.

### Repeating tasks

- Create daily, weekly, fortnightly, monthly or custom-interval tasks. Weekly schedules can include several weekdays. End on a date, after a session count, or choose **Never**.
- Each session is its own task, with its own status, transit journey, calendar event and completed-task contribution. Finite schedules support up to 500 sessions; months without the selected day (such as the 31st) are skipped.
- **Never** generates tasks four weeks ahead and extends that window when family tasks or My tasks are loaded. It does not depend on a scheduled worker.
- Claim **Every upcoming session** by default, **Just this date**, or **The next 4 sessions**. Whole-series claims also cover newly generated sessions. Other members cannot take an already claimed session or series.
- Give back one session when unavailable. That date becomes a permanent one-day exception; its replacement helper takes only that date. The original helper keeps the other sessions. Limited-scope claims also remain independent of later whole-series claims.
- Creators can edit only the selected date, that date and future sessions, or every upcoming session. Series edits preserve started/completed sessions and independent exceptions; time changes keep each session's calendar date. Moving to another date requires **Only this date**.
- Creators can pause/resume a series from Home or the recipient's Tasks tab. Pausing cancels attached future, unstarted sessions; resuming restores them and extends the window. Completed work and independent dates are preserved.
- Assistant claims/assignments follow the same whole-series default, while assistant edits, cancellation, completion and deletion act on the selected session. Deleted sessions are recorded so generation cannot recreate them.
- Recurring writes use MongoDB transactions and a unique series/occurrence index. Use **MongoDB Atlas or a replica set**; a standalone MongoDB server supports ordinary tasks but cannot create/change recurring series. Existing ordinary tasks need no migration.

### My tasks, transit and maps

- View your claimed tasks across families, filter by family, and switch between Upcoming, In progress and Done.
- See task progress, a week strip and due-soon/overdue indicators. Start, give back or complete tasks according to their current status.
- Follow journeys through **Departed home â†’ Arrived at clinic â†’ Consultation done â†’ Heading home â†’ Safely back home**.
- Post timestamped preset/custom milestones. The companion can remove mistakes, end transit without completing the task, or resume an eligible trip.
- Complete the task automatically when the companion records **Safely back home**.
- View the timeline and live position/path on a OneMap map. Location sharing requires the companion's browser permission and active transit page; it is not background phone tracking.
- Open location directions and follow trips as another member of the same family.

### Calendars

- Add individual tasks to Google Calendar or Outlook, or download an `.ics` event for Apple Calendar and compatible apps, without connecting an account.
- Optionally connect Google Calendar through OAuth from My tasks. Sync claimed, in-progress and completed tasks, update events, and remove events when tasks are given back or otherwise no longer belong in that calendar.
- Sync manually or through task-change/My tasks triggers. Disconnect with the option to remove generated events.
- Keep Google credentials and refresh tokens on the server; token fields are excluded from normal responses.

### Care logs, translation and voice input

- Write consultation, medication-change, diet, symptom and general notes in a recipient's Log tab.
- Record consultation details, next appointments and medication additions, adjustments or removals. Logs can reference related tasks.
- Filter and browse history. The author or family admin can edit/delete a note.
- Translate notes on demand into English, Chinese, Malay or Tamil using Azure Translator. Cache translations per language and invalidate them when the source content changes.
- Dictate notes using browser recording and Groq Whisper transcription. Review the transcription before saving; typed input remains available if recording/provider access fails.
- Choose whether to notify the family when creating a note.

### Telegram and updates

- Link a Telegram group with `/link <inviteCode>`, unlink with `/unlink`, and get instructions through `/start` or `/help`.
- Configure notification categories in Family settings. Admins can send a test message or unlink the group from the app.
- Generate notifications for task creation, claims/unclaims, completion/cancellation, transit milestones, care notes and medication updates where handlers call the shared notification utility.
- Store notification history with pending, sent, failed or skipped status, and display the history in Home's Recent updates.
- Omit clinical note bodies and medication details from generated Telegram messages. Task titles and user-provided text may still contain personal information.

### Contributions

- Separate leaderboard per family with **This week**, **This month** and **All time** views.
- Completed-task totals, helping members, care points, each person's task share, recent completions and a top-three podium.
- **Points:** 1 per completed task, +1 for an appointment requiring transit, +1 for claiming within one hour of task creation.
- Sort by points, completed-task count, name and account ID. Nonzero contributors receive consecutive ranks even when totals tie; zero-contribution members remain unranked.
- Show first place before second when only two people contributed; use the central first-place podium when three people contributed.
- Track consecutive helping-day streaks through today or yesterday across all time.
- Award period-based badges: **Appointment hero** for three completed appointments; **Quick to help** for three completed tasks claimed within an hour of creation; **Night owl** for five tasks completed after 6pm.
- Show Night owl progress and clickable contributor photos. Dates use Singapore time; weeks start Monday.
- Lock Contributions navigation for users without a family, with a hover/focus explanation.

### AI assistant and customisation

- Open a floating mascot assistant using your saved avatar appearance.
- Search family tasks and prepare proposals to create, edit, claim, assign, unclaim, start, complete, cancel or delete tasks through Gemini structured responses.
- Select a search result to retain that task as explicit chat context. Choosing Change time or Change location asks for the new value without a model-generated edit.
- Claim only for yourself; assign an open future task only if you created it, and only to a current family member. Start/complete only your assigned tasks, and cancel only tasks you created or are assigned to. Every write requires confirmation.
- Ask for missing details and present a confirmation card before writes. Deletion requires a second confirmation.
- Enforce family scope, current permissions, proposal expiry and stale-update checks on the server. Repeated confirmations do not create duplicate tasks.
- Clear chat on family/account changes. Messages stay in browser memory; task proposals are stored separately and expire after 15 minutes.
- Customise an Avatar Studio character with dresses, tops, skirts/shorts and accessories, and save the outfit to your account. The earlier pet dress-up screen is also retained.
- Available Avatar Studio characters include cat, dog, fox, elephant and dinosaur. Rabbit, chick and duck are locked as Coming soon.

## Task lifecycle and permissions

```text
open --claim before startAt--> claimed --start--> in_progress --complete--> completed
  ^                              |
  +----------- unclaim ----------+

open / claimed / in_progress --cancel--> cancelled
```

Completing directly from `claimed` is also supported. The transit `home` milestone uses the shared task-completion handler. **Overdue is a derived filter, not another stored status**: it identifies an unclaimed task whose scheduled start time has been reached.

| Action | Permission / restriction |
| --- | --- |
| Read family tasks, recipients, logs or trips | Authenticated family member |
| Claim | Family member; open task before its start time |
| Unclaim | Creator or claimer; task is still claimed |
| Start / complete | Claimer; valid current status required |
| Edit task | Creator; completed/cancelled tasks are locked |
| Delete task | Creator; in-progress/completed tasks cannot be deleted |
| Cancel task | Creator, assigned person or family admin; active tasks only. The assistant requires creator/assignee ownership |
| Add / edit recipient | Family member; only your own account can be newly linked |
| Archive recipient | Family admin |
| Edit / delete care log | Author or family admin |
| Manage other members, invitations or Telegram settings | Family admin; last-admin protection applies |

Admin status alone does not allow editing/deleting someone else's task or starting it on their behalf.

## Technology and structure

| Area | Implementation |
| --- | --- |
| Frontend | Vue 3, Vue Router, Vite, Bootstrap, Bootstrap Icons, Axios |
| Shared server data | TanStack Vue Query with family-scoped cache keys |
| Backend | Node.js ES modules, Express |
| Database | MongoDB, Mongoose |
| Authentication | bcryptjs, JWT, token-version revocation |
| Integrations | OneMap, Google Calendar, Telegram, Azure Translator, Groq Whisper, Gemini |
| Testing | Node test runner, Vitest, Vue Test Utils, jsdom, isolated MongoDB, Playwright |

```text
CareCircle/
  client/
    public/avatars/       Profile pictures, characters and wardrobe assets
    src/
      components/         Shared avatars, dialogs, cards and layout
      composables/        Active family, recipients and task cache
      features/           auth, family, settings, recipients, tasks, my-tasks,
                          transit, logs, contributions, assistant and avatar
      router/             Authenticated routes and isolated preview routes
      services/           HTTP client and query cache
      styles/             Themes and responsive layout
  server/
    src/
      features/           Models, controllers, services and feature routers
      middleware/         Authentication, membership and role checks
      routes/             API registration
      config/             Database connection
      utils/              Shared notifications and picture validation
    test/support/         Isolated database and provider fixtures
  tests/
    unit/                 Node regressions
    integration/          Express + isolated MongoDB tests
    e2e/                  Desktop/mobile browser workflows
    support/              Test-only application launcher
  docs/                   Contracts, ownership, design and testing notes
```

Backend `journeys/` implements transit sessions; the frontend calls it `transit/`. Persistent data includes users, families, recipients, tasks, recurring series, transit sessions, care logs, notifications, assistant proposals and Google Calendar links. Shared recurrence/calendar arithmetic lives in `shared/`. Account/integration records are user-scoped; family records are family-scoped and membership-protected.

## Local setup

Use **Node.js 24 LTS**, npm and a reachable MongoDB instance (Atlas or a replica set for repeating tasks). Core accounts, families, tasks and care profiles do not require optional integration credentials.

```sh
git clone https://github.com/SuMyatMyatHtay/CareCircle.git
cd CareCircle
npm install
npm install --prefix client
npm install --prefix server
```

The repository also contains pnpm lockfiles. Use one package manager consistently within each dependency directory. Do not run npm over a pnpm-created `node_modules` tree; start with a clean dependency directory when switching package managers.

Create `server/.env` from the updated [server/.env.example](server/.env.example). For a new checkout, copy the template using one of these commands:

```powershell
# Windows PowerShell (run from the repository root)
Copy-Item server/.env.example server/.env
```

```sh
# macOS / Linux (run from the repository root)
cp server/.env.example server/.env
```

If `server/.env` already exists, update its settings in place instead of overwriting it. Every template value is `REPLACE_THIS_WITH_YOUR_ACTUAL_VALUE`; these are placeholders, not working defaults. Core setup needs:

```dotenv
PORT=3000
MONGODB_URI=mongodb://127.0.0.1:27017/carecircle
JWT_SECRET=replace_with_a_long_random_secret
```

Use your actual MongoDB connection URI and a long random JWT secret. `PORT` must be a number, such as `3000`. The normal database connection explicitly uses the `carecircle` database. Tests use a separate generated database.

The template also includes all optional integration variables documented below. Replace the placeholders for integrations you use; leave unused optional variables empty or remove them. Placeholder strings can otherwise make an integration appear configured even though its credentials are invalid. For `GEMINI_MODEL`, supply a model ID available to your Gemini project, or leave it empty/remove it to use the default in `server/src/features/assistant/gemini.js`.

Create `client/.env`:

```dotenv
VITE_API_URL=http://localhost:3000/api
```

Set this explicitly because some account/family adapters read it directly. Restart the relevant development server after changing environment variables. Keep real credentials out of source control and out of `VITE_*` variables, which are included in the frontend bundle.

```sh
npm run dev
```

| Service | Address |
| --- | --- |
| Frontend | http://localhost:5173 |
| API | http://localhost:3000/api |
| Server health, without a DB connection | http://localhost:3000/api/health |
| Database health | http://localhost:3000/api/health/db |
| Fictional dashboard preview | http://localhost:5173/preview/home |

Start separately with `npm run dev:client` or `npm run dev:server`. Build the frontend with `npm run build`; serve the backend with `npm start --prefix server`.

The preview bypasses login and uses fictional local data; it does not validate real integrations. For a real workflow, register, create a family, add a recipient and post a future task. Join that family from another account using the invite code, claim the task, and open My tasks. Enable **Needs transit** on an appointment to test a real journey after starting it. Use fictional care information for demonstrations.

### Optional integration settings

The updated `server/.env.example` groups settings for Groq, Google Calendar, Gemini, Telegram, the frontend URL and Azure Translator. Configure the integrations you use in `server/.env`; keep provider credentials on the server.

| Feature | Variables | Additional setup |
| --- | --- | --- |
| AI assistant | `GEMINI_API_KEY`, optional `GEMINI_MODEL` | Choose a structured-output model available to your project; the code supplies a default |
| Care-log translation | `AZURE_TRANSLATOR_KEY`, `AZURE_TRANSLATOR_REGION` | Use the region belonging to your Translator resource |
| Voice notes | `GROQ_API_KEY` | Microphone permission; HTTPS or localhost for browser recording |
| Google Calendar sync | `GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID`, `GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET`, `GOOGLE_REDIRECT_URI` | Enable Calendar API and configure OAuth consent/test users and the exact callback URI |
| Telegram | `TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN`, `TELEGRAM_WEBHOOK_SECRET`, optional `TELEGRAM_BOT_USERNAME` | Register a public webhook at `/api/integrations/telegram/webhook` with the matching secret token |
| Telegram task links | `APP_URL` | Frontend origin, e.g. `http://localhost:5173` locally |
| OneMap search and maps | No credentials in the current implementation | Network access; location permission for live sharing |

For local Google OAuth, use `http://localhost:5173/api/google/callback` as the callback: Vite proxies `/api` to port 3000, and the callback returns to the frontend origin. Register the same URI in Google and `GOOGLE_REDIRECT_URI`.

For Telegram, add the bot to a group and send `/link YOUR_INVITE_CODE`. Family settings provides notification preferences, test delivery and unlinking. A local backend needs a public HTTPS endpoint/tunnel for webhook delivery.

For deployment, build `client/` to `dist/`, configure its API URL at build time, and configure backend variables separately. The client includes a Vercel SPA rewrite. The backend exports the Express app for serverless hosting and otherwise listens on `PORT`.

## API overview

Paths below are relative to `/api`. [server/src/routes/index.js](server/src/routes/index.js) registers the current endpoints.

| Prefix | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `/auth` | Registration, sessions, current/public profiles, avatar/pet saving |
| `/families` | Create/join/list families; members, roles and invitations |
| `/families/:familyId/recipients` | Recipient profiles and archiving |
| `/families/:familyId/tasks` | CRUD, claim/unclaim, start, complete and cancel |
| `/families/:familyId/tasks/recurring` | List recurring series; `PATCH /:seriesId` pauses/resumes a creator's series |
| `/families/:familyId/tasks/:taskId/transit` | Session, milestones, location, end/resume |
| `/families/:familyId/transit` | Family transit sessions |
| `/families/:familyId/logs` | Care logs and translation |
| `/families/:familyId/notifications` | Family notification history |
| `/families/:familyId/notify-settings` | Telegram preferences, test delivery and unlinking |
| `/families/:familyId/assistant` | Chat and confirm/cancel task proposals |
| `/me/tasks` | Signed-in person's tasks across families |
| `/me/google`, `/google/callback` | Calendar connection, sync and OAuth callback |
| `/integrations` | OneMap search, voice transcription and Telegram webhook |

Contributions is calculated from existing membership-protected task/member endpoints; there is no separate Contributions API. See [API-CONTRACT.md](docs/API-CONTRACT.md) for detailed contracts, and feature routes when older design notes differ from the implementation.

## Testing

From the repository root:

```sh
npm test
npm run build
```

| Command | Coverage |
| --- | --- |
| `npm run test:regression` | All Node regressions in `tests/unit/*.test.mjs` |
| `npm run test:unit` | Alias for Node unit/regression tests |
| `npm run test:support` | Test infrastructure isolation guards and fixture helpers |
| `npm run test:client` | Vitest functions, components and page integration |
| `npm run test:api` | Express/JWT/Mongoose against isolated real MongoDB |
| `npm run test:integration` | Alias for API/database integration tests |
| `npm run test:e2e` | Desktop/mobile Chromium workflows |
| `npm run test:e2e:headed` | Browser workflows in visible windows |
| `npm run test:all` | Node, frontend, API and browser suites in sequence |
| `npm run test:watch --prefix client` | Frontend watch mode |

Before browser tests, install Chromium using `npx playwright install chromium`. API/E2E tests may download a MongoDB binary on their first run. E2E reserves frontend port **5180**; its API and database use available local ports.

Recurring-task API/E2E tests use a local replica set for transaction support. See [the current testing commands and setup](docs/TESTING-RECURRING.md) for focused commands, support helpers, prerequisites and verified/unverified results.

The API/E2E harness generates a loopback `carecircle_test_*` database, validates isolation before resets, and does not load `server/.env` or run the shared seed script. External providers are disabled or doubled where appropriate. Tests cover family isolation, roles, sessions, claims/conflicts, overdue deadlines, unclaiming, recipient preservation, contributions, profile links, assistant confirmation, transit, calendar helpers and translation. Isolated tests do not prove live provider or deployment configuration.

See [docs/TESTING.md](docs/TESTING.md), [docs/TESTING-PART-E.md](docs/TESTING-PART-E.md) and [tests/e2e/README.md](tests/e2e/README.md). Use command output for current totals; counts in older documents are historical.

## Current limitations

- The sidebar **Calendar** entry remains Coming soon. Calendar export, Google Calendar sync and the mobile settings agenda are separate implemented features.
- The conventional task-detail **Edit** button for ordinary tasks is a placeholder; recurring tasks have a scoped editing dialog. Creator-authorised task updates are also available through the API and assistant proposals. Cancellation has an API route, without a complete task-detail cancellation UI.
- Family names are set at creation and cannot be changed. Member roles support admin/member; custom relationship labels are not supported.
- Dashboard, notifications and transit use polling rather than Socket.IO. Live location requires the companion's active page and browser permission.
- There is no scheduled reminder worker. Open-ended recurrence extends on task reads, so a family that never loads tasks does not generate more sessions automatically. Due-soon indicators, event-triggered Telegram notifications and calendar reminders are distinct from scheduled CareCircle reminders; recurring tasks do not add evening-before Telegram reminders.
- The assistant enforces task ownership and status rules for every confirmed action. Its quota is per server process. It sends task context/user messages to Gemini and does not provide medical advice.
- A yearly contribution wrap, the deferred gratitude log and locked avatar characters are not implemented features.

## Contributing

Work on a feature branch and submit a pull request describing the change, validation and screenshots for UI changes. Keep code within its feature folders, coordinate shared schema/API changes with the owner, and update affected contracts alongside code. Check desktop/mobile, loading, empty, success and failure states. Do not reseed the shared database without coordinating with the team.

Further notes: [family UI](docs/FAMILY-UI.md), [assistant](docs/ASSISTANT.md), [database design](docs/DATABASE-DESIGN.md) and [ownership](docs/OWNERSHIP.md). Some notes describe earlier plans; implemented routes and source code take precedence when they differ.

    "test": "npm run test:regression && npm run test:support && npm run test:client",
    "test:unit": "npm run test:regression",
    "test:support": "node --test tests/support/*.test.mjs",
    "test:integration": "npm run test:api",
    "test:regression": "node --test tests/unit/*.test.mjs",
    "test:client": "npm run test --prefix client",
    "test:api": "node --test tests/integration/*.test.mjs",
    "test:e2e": "playwright test",
    "test:e2e:headed": "playwright test --headed",
    "test:all": "npm test && npm run test:api && npm run test:e2e",
    "test:settings": "node --test tests/unit/family-settings.test.mjs tests/unit/settings-account.test.mjs",

FILE: client/index.html
================================================
<!doctype html>
<html lang="en">
  <head>
    <meta charset="UTF-8" />
    <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1.0" />
    <title>CareCircle</title>
    <script>
      // Apply the saved theme before the Vue bundle loads to avoid a light flash.
      (() => {
        let choice = 'light'
        try { choice = localStorage.getItem('carecircle:appearance') || 'light' } catch {}
        const theme = choice === 'dark' ||
          (choice === 'system' && matchMedia('(prefers-color-scheme: dark)').matches)
          ? 'dark' : 'light'
        document.documentElement.dataset.theme = theme
        document.documentElement.dataset.bsTheme = theme
      })()
    </script>
    <style>
      html { background: #fafaf7; color-scheme: light; }
      html[data-theme='dark'] { background: #141a17; color-scheme: dark; }
    </style>
    <link rel="preconnect" href="https://fonts.googleapis.com" />
    <link href="https://fonts.googleapis.com/css2?family=Inter:wght@400;500;600;700&family=Nunito:wght@400;700;800;900&display=swap" rel="stylesheet" />
  </head>
  <body>
    <div id="app"></div>
    <script type="module" src="/src/main.js"></script>
  </body>
</html>

<script setup>
import { computed, ref, watch } from 'vue'
import { defaultProfilePicture } from './profilePictures.js'
const props = defineProps({
  person: { type: Object, default: () => ({}) },
  size: { type: String, default: 'normal' },
})
const failed = ref(false)
const picture = computed(() => props.person.profilePicture || defaultProfilePicture(props.person))
watch(picture, () => { failed.value = false })
</script>

<template>
  <span class="care-avatar" :class="`care-avatar--${size}`" aria-hidden="true">
    <img :src="failed ? defaultProfilePicture(person) : picture" alt="" @error="failed = true" />
  </span>
</template>

<script setup>
import { onMounted, onUnmounted, ref } from 'vue'
import { useAnimatedClose } from '../../composables/useAnimatedClose.js'
defineProps({ title: { type: String, required: true } })
const emit = defineEmits(['close'])
const panel = ref(null)
// Escape, the backdrop and the close button all fade the dialog out before 'close'
const { closing, requestClose, onAnimationEnd } = useAnimatedClose(() => emit('close'))
let previousFocus
function onKeydown(event) {
  if (event.key === 'Escape') requestClose()
  if (event.key !== 'Tab') return
  const controls = [
    ...panel.value.querySelectorAll(
      'button:not(:disabled), input:not(:disabled), select:not(:disabled), textarea:not(:disabled), a[href], [tabindex="0"]',
    ),
  ].filter((node) => node.getClientRects().length)
  const first = controls[0],
    last = controls.at(-1)
  if (!controls.length) {
    event.preventDefault()
    panel.value.focus()
  } else if (document.activeElement === panel.value) {
    event.preventDefault()
    const target = event.shiftKey ? last : first
    target?.focus()
  } else if (event.shiftKey && document.activeElement === first) {
    event.preventDefault()
    last?.focus()
  } else if (!event.shiftKey && document.activeElement === last) {
    event.preventDefault()
    first?.focus()
  }
}
onMounted(() => {
  previousFocus = document.activeElement
  panel.value.focus()
  document.addEventListener('keydown', onKeydown)
})
onUnmounted(() => {
  document.removeEventListener('keydown', onKeydown)
  previousFocus?.focus()
})
</script>

<template>
  <!-- Parents mount this with v-if, so it animates in with appear and out with `closing` -->

<script setup>
import { computed, inject } from 'vue'
import { RouterLink, routeLocationKey } from 'vue-router'
import CareAvatar from './CareAvatar.vue'
const props = defineProps({
  person: { type: Object, default: () => ({}) },
  size: { type: String, default: 'normal' },
  recipient: Boolean,
})
const route = inject(routeLocationKey, null)
const idOf = value => value?._id || value?.id || (typeof value === 'string' ? value : '')
const target = computed(() => {
  if (!route || route.meta.preview) return null
  const userId = props.recipient ? idOf(props.person.linkedUser) : idOf(props.person)
  if (userId) {
    let ownId = ''
    try { ownId = JSON.parse(sessionStorage.getItem('user') || '{}').id } catch { /* no cached account */ }
    return userId === ownId ? '/profile' : `/profile/${encodeURIComponent(userId)}`
  }
  const recipientId = props.recipient && idOf(props.person)
  return recipientId ? `/recipients/${encodeURIComponent(recipientId)}/profile` : null
})
const label = computed(() => `View ${props.person.nickname || props.person.name || 'member'}'s profile`)
</script>

  <RouterLink v-if="target" :to="target" class="care-profile-avatar-link" :aria-label="label" :title="label" @click.stop><CareAvatar :person="person" :size="size" /></RouterLink>
  <CareAvatar v-else :person="person" :size="size" />
</template>

<script setup>
import { ref, nextTick, onBeforeUnmount } from 'vue'
import CareAvatar from './CareAvatar.vue'
import { profilePictures } from './profilePictures.js'
const props = defineProps({ modelValue: { type: String, default: '' }, careType: { type: String, default: '' }, disabled: Boolean })
const emit = defineEmits(['update:modelValue'])
const error = ref('')
const dialog = ref(null), trigger = ref(null), fileInput = ref(null)
const draft = ref(''), processing = ref(false)
let uploadVersion = 0
async function open() {
  if (props.disabled) return
  draft.value = props.modelValue
  error.value = ''
  await nextTick()
  dialog.value.showModal()
}
function close() {
  uploadVersion++
  processing.value = false
  dialog.value?.close()
  trigger.value?.focus()
}
function apply() {
  if (props.disabled || processing.value) return
  emit('update:modelValue', draft.value)
  close()
}
onBeforeUnmount(() => { uploadVersion++; dialog.value?.close() })
async function upload(event) {
  error.value = ''
  const file = event.target.files?.[0]
  event.target.value = ''
  if (!file) return
  if (!['image/jpeg', 'image/png', 'image/webp'].includes(file.type) || file.size > 10 * 1024 * 1024) {
    error.value = 'Choose a JPG, PNG or WebP image under 10 MB.'; return
  }
  const version = ++uploadVersion
  processing.value = true
  const url = URL.createObjectURL(file)
  try {
    const image = new Image()
    image.src = url
    await image.decode()
    const canvas = document.createElement('canvas')
    canvas.width = canvas.height = 160
    const ctx = canvas.getContext('2d')
    ctx.fillStyle = '#fff'; ctx.fillRect(0, 0, 160, 160)
    const side = Math.min(image.width, image.height)
    ctx.drawImage(image, (image.width-side)/2, (image.height-side)/2, side, side, 0, 0, 160, 160)
    const data = canvas.toDataURL('image/jpeg', 0.8)
    if (data.length > 50000) throw new Error('Image too large')
    if (version === uploadVersion && !props.disabled) draft.value = data
  } catch { if (version === uploadVersion) error.value = 'Unable to read this image. Please try another picture.' }
  finally { URL.revokeObjectURL(url); if (version === uploadVersion) processing.value = false }
}
</script>
<template>
  <button ref="trigger" type="button" class="picture-trigger" :disabled="disabled" aria-label="Change profile picture" aria-haspopup="dialog" @click="open">
    <CareAvatar :person="{ profilePicture: modelValue, careType }" size="profile" />
    <span class="picture-camera"><i class="bi bi-camera-fill" aria-hidden="true"></i></span>

    <dialog ref="dialog" class="picture-dialog" aria-label="Change profile picture" @cancel.prevent.stop="close" @keydown.esc.stop.prevent="close" @click="($event.target === dialog) && close()">

        <button type="button" class="picture-upload" :disabled="processing || disabled" @click="fileInput.click()"><i class="bi bi-upload" aria-hidden="true"></i>{{ processing ? 'Preparing photo?' : 'Upload a photo' }}</button>

FILE: client/src/components/common/__tests__/ProfileAvatar.spec.js
================================================
import { describe, it, expect } from 'vitest'
import { mount, flushPromises } from '@vue/test-utils'
import { createMemoryHistory, createRouter } from 'vue-router'
import ProfileAvatar from '../ProfileAvatar.vue'

async function avatar(props, preview = false) {
  const router = createRouter({ history: createMemoryHistory(), routes: [
    { path: '/home', component: { template: '<div />' }, meta: { preview } },
    { path: '/profile', component: { template: '<div />' } },
    { path: '/profile/:userId', component: { template: '<div />' } },
    { path: '/recipients/:recipientId/profile', component: { template: '<div />' } },
  ] })
  await router.push('/home')
  const wrapper = mount(ProfileAvatar, { props, global: { plugins: [router] } })
  return { wrapper, router }
}
describe('Avatar profile links', () => {
  it('opens the correct member profile when clicked', async () => {
    const { wrapper, router } = await avatar({ person: { _id: 'jasmine', name: 'Jasmine' } })
    expect(wrapper.get('a').attributes('aria-label')).toBe("View Jasmine's profile")
    await wrapper.get('a').trigger('click')
    await flushPromises()
    expect(router.currentRoute.value.path).toBe('/profile/jasmine')
  })
  it('opens my own profile for my avatar', async () => {
    sessionStorage.setItem('user', JSON.stringify({ id: 'alex' }))
    const { wrapper } = await avatar({ person: { id: 'alex', name: 'Alex' } })
    expect(wrapper.get('a').attributes('href')).toBe('/profile')
  })
  it('uses linked account identity instead of the recipient record id', async () => {
    const { wrapper } = await avatar({ recipient: true, person: { _id: 'recipient-one', linkedUser: { _id: 'jasmine' }, name: 'Jasmine' } })
    expect(wrapper.get('a').attributes('href')).toBe('/profile/jasmine')
  })
  it('opens a care profile when the recipient has no account', async () => {
    const { wrapper } = await avatar({ recipient: true, person: { _id: 'grandpa', name: 'Grandpa' } })
    expect(wrapper.get('a').attributes('href')).toBe('/recipients/grandpa/profile')
  })
  it('does not invent links for unidentified people or preview accounts', async () => {
    const unknown = await avatar({ person: { name: 'Family' } })
    expect(unknown.wrapper.find('a').exists()).toBe(false)
    const preview = await avatar({ person: { _id: 'sample', name: 'Sample' } }, true)
    expect(preview.wrapper.find('a').exists()).toBe(false)
  })
})

// Shared "which family am I looking at" state for every logged-in page.
// The state lives at module level, so every component that calls
// useActiveFamily() sees the same families and the same selection.
//
//   const { selectedFamilyId } = useActiveFamily()
//   http.get(`/families/${selectedFamilyId.value}/tasks`)

import { ref, computed } from 'vue'
import {
  getMyFamilies,
  getFamilyErrorMessage,
} from '../features/family/services/familyApi.js'

const families = ref([])
const selectedFamilyId = ref(sessionStorage.getItem('activeFamilyId') || '')
const isLoading = ref(false)
const errorMessage = ref('')
let requestVersion = 0
let familySessionToken = sessionStorage.getItem('token') || ''

const selectedFamily = computed(
  () => families.value.find((f) => f.id === selectedFamilyId.value) || null,
)

// Load the logged-in user's families and keep the previous selection if it is still valid
async function loadFamilies() {
  const version = ++requestVersion
  const requestToken = sessionStorage.getItem('token') || ''
  const isCurrent = () =>
    version === requestVersion &&
    requestToken === (sessionStorage.getItem('token') || '')
  // Do not show a previous account's cached families during a new sign-in.
  if (requestToken !== familySessionToken) {
    families.value = []
    selectedFamilyId.value = sessionStorage.getItem('activeFamilyId') || ''
  }
  familySessionToken = requestToken
  isLoading.value = true
  errorMessage.value = ''

  try {
    const result = await getMyFamilies()
    if (!isCurrent()) return
    if (!Array.isArray(result)) {
      throw new Error('Invalid family data from server.')
    }

    families.value = result
    const stillMine = result.some((f) => f.id === selectedFamilyId.value)
    selectFamily(stillMine ? selectedFamilyId.value : result[0]?.id || '')
  } catch (error) {
    if (!isCurrent()) return
    errorMessage.value = getFamilyErrorMessage(error)
    families.value = []
    selectFamily('')
  } finally {
    if (version === requestVersion) isLoading.value = false
  }
}

function selectFamily(familyId) {
  selectedFamilyId.value = familyId
  if (familyId) sessionStorage.setItem('activeFamilyId', familyId)
  else sessionStorage.removeItem('activeFamilyId')
}

// Call on logout so the next user doesn't see the previous user's families
function clearFamilies() {
  requestVersion++
  familySessionToken = sessionStorage.getItem('token') || ''
  families.value = []
  isLoading.value = false
  errorMessage.value = ''
  selectFamily('')
}

export function useActiveFamily() {
  return {
    families,
    selectedFamilyId,
    selectedFamily,
    isLoading,
    errorMessage,
    loadFamilies,
    selectFamily,
    clearFamilies,
  }
}

FILE: client/src/composables/useAnimatedClose.js
================================================
// Lets a modal play its closing animation before the parent removes it with v-if.
// requestClose() adds the closing classes; once the panel's animation ends (or after
// the fallback, e.g. under "Reduce motion" where there is no animation) onClosed runs.
//
//   const { closing, requestClose, onAnimationEnd } = useAnimatedClose(() => emit('close'))
//   <section :class="{ 'care-pop-closing': closing }" @animationend="onAnimationEnd">
import { ref, onUnmounted } from 'vue'

export function useAnimatedClose(onClosed, fallbackMs = 200) {
  const closing = ref(false)
  let timer = null
  let done = false

  function finish() {
    if (done) return
    done = true
    clearTimeout(timer)
    onClosed()
  }

  function requestClose() {
    if (closing.value) return
    closing.value = true
    timer = setTimeout(finish, fallbackMs)
  }

  // Only the panel's own closing animation counts, not one bubbling up from a child
  function onAnimationEnd(event) {
    if (closing.value && event.target === event.currentTarget) finish()
  }

  onUnmounted(() => clearTimeout(timer))

  return { closing, requestClose, onAnimationEnd }
}

import { onMounted, onUnmounted, toValue } from 'vue'

// Accept a ref or getter so a list can identify its currently open menu.
export function useDismissibleMenu(root, dismiss) {
  function outside(event) {
    const element = toValue(root)
    if (element && !element.contains(event.target)) dismiss()
  }
  function escape(event) {
    const element = toValue(root)
    if (event.key !== 'Escape' || !element) return
    dismiss()
    element.querySelector('button')?.focus({ preventScroll: true })
  }
  onMounted(() => {
    document.addEventListener('pointerdown', outside, true)
    document.addEventListener('focusin', outside)
    document.addEventListener('keydown', escape)
  })
  onUnmounted(() => {
    document.removeEventListener('pointerdown', outside, true)
    document.removeEventListener('focusin', outside)
    document.removeEventListener('keydown', escape)
  })
}

FILE: client/src/composables/useFamilyTasks.js

// Owner: Marcus (D)
// The selected family's tasks, cached with TanStack Query. Family home, the
// recipient Overview and the recipient Tasks tab all read this one list and
// filter it themselves, so moving between them doesn't refetch.
//
//   const { tasks, isLoading, errorMessage } = useFamilyTasks()
//   const mine = computed(() => tasks.value.filter((t) => taskRecipientId(t) === id))
//
// After changing a task, update the cache instead of refetching:
//   const { upsertTask, removeTask } = useTaskCache()
//   upsertTask(familyId, updatedTask)   // claim, edit, create, socket events...

import { computed, toValue } from 'vue'
import { useQuery, useQueryClient } from '@tanstack/vue-query'
import { useActiveFamily } from './useActiveFamily.js'
import { queryKeys } from '../services/queryClient.js'
import { getFamilyTasks, getTaskErrorMessage } from '../features/tasks/services/tasksApi.js'

// A task's recipient comes back populated ({ _id, name }) or as a bare id
export function taskRecipientId(task) {
    return task.recipient?._id ?? task.recipient ?? null
}

export function useFamilyTasks({ enabled = true } = {}) {
    const { selectedFamilyId } = useActiveFamily()

    const query = useQuery({
        queryKey: computed(() => queryKeys.tasks(selectedFamilyId.value)),
        queryFn: ({ queryKey }) => getFamilyTasks(queryKey[1]),
        enabled: computed(() => Boolean(toValue(enabled) && selectedFamilyId.value))
    })

    const tasks = computed(() => query.data.value ?? [])

    // Only show an error when there is nothing to show instead. If a background
    // refetch fails, keep showing the tasks we already have.
    const errorMessage = computed(() =>
        query.error.value && !query.data.value ? getTaskErrorMessage(query.error.value) : ''
    )

    return {
        tasks,
        isLoading: query.isLoading,
        isFetching: query.isFetching,
        errorMessage,
        refetch: query.refetch
    }
}

// Write task changes straight into the cache, so every page updates at once
export function useTaskCache() {
    const queryClient = useQueryClient()

    function upsertTask(familyId, task) {
        queryClient.setQueryData(queryKeys.tasks(familyId), (old) => {
            if (!old) return old
            const exists = old.some((t) => t._id === task._id)
            const next = exists ? old.map((t) => (t._id === task._id ? task : t)) : [...old, task]
            return next.sort((a, b) => new Date(a.startAt) - new Date(b.startAt))
        })
    }

    function removeTask(familyId, taskId) {
        queryClient.setQueryData(queryKeys.tasks(familyId), (old) => old?.filter((t) => t._id !== taskId))
    }

    function invalidateTasks(familyId) {
        return queryClient.invalidateQueries({ queryKey: queryKeys.tasks(familyId) })
    }

    return { upsertTask, removeTask, invalidateTasks }
}

FILE: client/src/composables/useRecipients.js

// The selected family's care recipients (package C), cached with TanStack Query.
// The sidebar, Family home and the recipient pages all read the same cached list,
// and it follows the family picked in the sidebar on its own.
// Call refresh() after a create, edit or archive so every place updates.
//
//   const { recipients, isLoading, errorMessage, refresh } = useRecipients()
//   const { recipient, notFound, setRecipient } = useRecipient(recipientIdRef)

import { computed, toValue } from 'vue'
import { useQuery, useQueryClient } from '@tanstack/vue-query'
import { useActiveFamily } from './useActiveFamily.js'
import { queryKeys } from '../services/queryClient.js'
import { getRecipients, getRecipient, getRecipientErrorMessage } from '../features/recipients/services/recipientsApi.js'

export function useRecipients({ enabled = true } = {}) {
    const { selectedFamilyId } = useActiveFamily()
    const queryClient = useQueryClient()

    const query = useQuery({
        queryKey: computed(() => queryKeys.recipientList(selectedFamilyId.value)),
        queryFn: ({ queryKey }) => getRecipients(queryKey[1]),
        enabled: computed(() => Boolean(toValue(enabled) && selectedFamilyId.value))
    })

    const recipients = computed(() => query.data.value ?? [])
    const errorMessage = computed(() =>
        query.error.value && !query.data.value ? getRecipientErrorMessage(query.error.value) : ''
    )

    // Refetch the list and every cached recipient of this family
    function refresh() {
        return queryClient.invalidateQueries({ queryKey: queryKeys.recipients(selectedFamilyId.value) })
    }

    return {
        recipients,
        isLoading: query.isLoading,
        errorMessage,
        refresh
    }
}

// One recipient, for the recipient hub. Shows the copy from the cached list straight
// away (if there is one) while the full record loads.
export function useRecipient(recipientId) {
    const { selectedFamilyId } = useActiveFamily()
    const queryClient = useQueryClient()

    const query = useQuery({
        queryKey: computed(() => queryKeys.recipient(selectedFamilyId.value, recipientId.value)),
        queryFn: ({ queryKey }) => getRecipient(queryKey[1], queryKey[4]),
        enabled: computed(() => Boolean(selectedFamilyId.value && recipientId.value)),
        placeholderData: () =>
            queryClient
                .getQueryData(queryKeys.recipientList(selectedFamilyId.value))
                ?.find((r) => r._id === recipientId.value)
    })

    const notFound = computed(() => query.error.value?.response?.status === 404)
    const errorMessage = computed(() =>
        query.error.value && !notFound.value && !query.data.value ? getRecipientErrorMessage(query.error.value) : ''
    )

    // Put a saved recipient straight into the cache (e.g. after editing the profile)
    function setRecipient(updated) {
        queryClient.setQueryData(queryKeys.recipient(selectedFamilyId.value, updated._id), updated)
    }

    return {
        recipient: computed(() => query.data.value ?? null),
        isLoading: query.isLoading,
        notFound,
        errorMessage,
        refetch: query.refetch,
        setRecipient
    }
}

FILE: client/src/composables/useTabIndicator.js
================================================
// One underline that slides to the active tab instead of jumping between tabs.
// The tab bar needs position: relative; the active tab needs the class `active`.
//
//   const tabBar = ref(null)
//   const indicator = useTabIndicator(tabBar, () => activeTab.value)
//   <div ref="tabBar" class="tabs">
//     ...tabs...
//     <span class="care-tab-indicator" :class="{ 'is-ready': indicator.ready }"
//         :style="indicator.style" aria-hidden="true"></span>
//   </div>
import { reactive, watch, nextTick, onUnmounted } from 'vue'

export function useTabIndicator(tabBar, activeKey) {
  const indicator = reactive({ style: { width: '0px', opacity: 0 }, ready: false })
  let observer = null

  function measure() {
    const active = tabBar.value?.querySelector('.active')
    if (!active) {
      indicator.style = { ...indicator.style, opacity: 0 }
      return
    }
    indicator.style = {
      width: `${active.offsetWidth}px`,
      transform: `translateX(${active.offsetLeft}px)`,
      opacity: 1,
    }
  }

  function stopWatchingSize() {
    observer?.disconnect()
    observer = null
    window.removeEventListener('resize', measure)
  }

  // The tab bar can come and go (e.g. My tasks swaps to its phone layout), so follow the ref
  watch(
    tabBar,
    (bar) => {
      stopWatchingSize()
      indicator.ready = false
      if (!bar) return
      measure()
      // Slide only after the first position is set, so it doesn't fly in from the left
      requestAnimationFrame(() => {
        indicator.ready = true
      })
      // Tab widths change on resize and when the web font loads
      if (typeof ResizeObserver === 'undefined') {
        window.addEventListener('resize', measure)
        return
      }
      observer = new ResizeObserver(measure)
      observer.observe(bar)
      for (const tab of bar.children) {
        if (!tab.classList.contains('care-tab-indicator')) observer.observe(tab)
      }
    },
    { flush: 'post', immediate: true },
  )

  // The active tab turns bold, so measure after it re-renders
  watch(activeKey, () => nextTick(measure))

  onUnmounted(stopWatchingSize)

  return indicator
}

FILE: client/src/features/assistant/composables/useAssistantChat.js
================================================
import { ref, computed, watch, onBeforeUnmount, toValue } from 'vue'
import { useQueryClient } from '@tanstack/vue-query'
import { queryKeys } from '../../../services/queryClient.js'
import { useFamilyWorkspace } from '../../family/composables/useFamilyWorkspace.js'
import { useTaskCache } from '../../../composables/useFamilyTasks.js'
import { sendAssistantMessage, confirmAssistantProposal, cancelAssistantProposal, assistantErrorMessage } from '../services/assistantApi.js'

export function conversationPayload(messages) {
  const recent = []
  let length = 0
  for (const message of [...messages].reverse()) {
    const metadata = message.proposal ? `\nTask proposal (${message.proposalState || 'pending'}): ${JSON.stringify(message.proposal)}`
      : message.tasks?.length ? `\nMatching tasks: ${JSON.stringify(message.tasks)}` : ''
    const content = (message.content + metadata).slice(0, 6000)
    if (recent.length >= 24 || length + content.length > 22000) break
    recent.unshift({ role: message.role, content })
    length += content.length
  }
  // A user-first window keeps conversation roles compatible with Gemini.
  while (recent.length && recent[0].role !== 'user') recent.shift()
  return recent
}

export function useAssistantChat(user) {
  const { selectedFamilyId, selectedFamily } = useFamilyWorkspace()
  const { upsertTask, removeTask, invalidateTasks } = useTaskCache()
  const queryClient = useQueryClient()
  const messages = ref([]), input = ref(''), busy = ref(false), error = ref(''), retryable = ref(false)
  const selectedTaskId = ref('')
  const editField = ref('')
  let selectingTask = false
  let version = 0, controller
  const canSend = computed(() => Boolean(selectedFamilyId.value && input.value.trim() && !busy.value))
  function reset() {
    version++; controller?.abort()
    messages.value = []; input.value = ''; error.value = ''; busy.value = false; retryable.value = false
    selectedTaskId.value = ''; editField.value = ''; selectingTask = false
  }
  watch([selectedFamilyId, () => toValue(user)?.id], reset)
  onBeforeUnmount(() => { version++; controller?.abort() })
  function begin() {
    controller?.abort(); controller = new AbortController()
    const requestVersion = ++version, token = sessionStorage.getItem('token'), familyId = selectedFamilyId.value
    busy.value = true; error.value = ''; retryable.value = false
    return { familyId, signal: controller.signal,
      current: () => requestVersion === version && token === sessionStorage.getItem('token') && familyId === selectedFamilyId.value,
      finish: () => {
        // A changed session must discard the reply, but still release this request's spinner.
        if (requestVersion !== version) return
        busy.value = false
        if (token !== sessionStorage.getItem('token')) {
          error.value = 'Your session changed. Start a new chat to continue.'
          retryable.value = false
        }
      } }
  }
  async function ask() {
    const request = begin()
    try {
      const result = await sendAssistantMessage(request.familyId, conversationPayload(messages.value), request.signal,
        selectedTaskId.value ? { selectedTaskId: selectedTaskId.value, selectTask: selectingTask, ...(editField.value ? { editField: editField.value } : {}) } : {})
      if (!request.current()) return
      selectingTask = false
      editField.value = result.editField || ''
      messages.value.push({ role: 'assistant', content: result.message, suggestions: result.suggestions || [],
        tasks: result.tasks || [], hasMore: result.hasMore, proposal: result.proposal, proposalState: result.proposal ? 'pending' : undefined })
    } catch (e) {
      if (request.current()) {
        const status = e.response?.status
        if ([400, 403, 404, 409, 410].includes(status)) {
          editField.value = ''
          messages.value.push({ role: 'assistant', content: assistantErrorMessage(e), suggestions: [] })
          retryable.value = false
        } else {
          error.value = assistantErrorMessage(e)
          retryable.value = e.code !== 'ERR_CANCELED' && (!status || status === 429 || status >= 500)
        }
      }
    } finally { request.finish() }
  }
  async function send(text = input.value) {
    if (busy.value || !selectedFamilyId.value || !text.trim()) return
    // A new message replaces the active draft; only the latest card can be confirmed.
    for (const message of messages.value) if (message.proposalState === 'pending') message.proposalState = 'replaced'
    messages.value.push({ role: 'user', content: text.trim().slice(0, 2000) })
    input.value = ''
    await ask()
  }
  async function selectTask(task) {
    if (busy.value || !task?.id) return
    selectedTaskId.value = task.id; editField.value = ''; selectingTask = true
    await send(`Selected task: ${task.title}. What can I do with this task?`)
  }
  async function confirm(message) {
    if (busy.value || message.proposalState !== 'pending') return
    const request = begin()
    try {
      const result = await confirmAssistantProposal(request.familyId, message.proposal.id, request.signal)
      if (!request.current()) return
      if (result.requiresSecondConfirmation) {
        message.proposal.deletionAcknowledged = true
        message.proposal.confirmationWarning = result.message
        return
      }
      message.proposalState = 'saved'
      await queryClient.cancelQueries({ queryKey: queryKeys.tasks(request.familyId) })
      if (!request.current()) return
      if (result.deleted) removeTask(request.familyId, result.taskId)
      else upsertTask(request.familyId, result.task)
      // Reconcile any in-flight fetch and refresh all visible task boards.
      void invalidateTasks(request.familyId)
      window.dispatchEvent(new CustomEvent('carecircle:task-updated', { detail: { familyId: request.familyId, task: result.task, taskId: result.taskId, deleted: result.deleted, action: message.proposal.action, title: message.proposal.task.title } }))
      const action = { create: 'Created', update: 'Updated', unclaim: 'Unclaimed', delete: 'Deleted', claim: 'Claimed', assign: 'Assigned', start: 'Started', complete: 'Completed', cancel: 'Cancelled' }[message.proposal.action]
      messages.value.push({ role: 'assistant', content: `${action}: ${result.task?.title || message.proposal.task.title}. Your task list is up to date.` })
    } catch (e) {
      if (request.current()) {
        error.value = assistantErrorMessage(e)
        if ([400, 403, 404, 409, 410].includes(e.response?.status)) message.proposalState = 'unavailable'
      }
    } finally { request.finish() }
  }
  async function dismiss(message) {
    if (busy.value || message.proposalState !== 'pending') return
    const request = begin()
    try {
      await cancelAssistantProposal(request.familyId, message.proposal.id, request.signal)
      if (request.current()) message.proposalState = 'cancelled'
    } catch (e) { if (request.current()) error.value = assistantErrorMessage(e) }
    finally { request.finish() }
  }
  async function retry() { if (!busy.value && retryable.value && selectedFamilyId.value) await ask() }
  function stop() { controller?.abort() }
  return { messages, input, busy, error, retryable, canSend, selectedFamilyId, selectedFamily, send, selectTask, confirm, dismiss, retry, reset, stop }
}

FILE: client/src/features/assistant/services/assistantApi.js

import { http } from '../../../services/http.js'

async function post(familyId, path, body, signal) {
  const token = sessionStorage.getItem('token')
  if (!token) throw new Error('Please log in again to use the assistant.')
  // A wall-clock deadline also covers connections that never reach Axios's response timer.
  const deadline = AbortSignal.timeout(55000)
  try {
    const response = await http.post(`/families/${familyId}/assistant/${path}`, body, {
      signal: signal ? AbortSignal.any([signal, deadline]) : deadline,
      timeout: 55000, headers: { Authorization: `Bearer ${token}` }
    })
    return response.data
  } catch (error) {
    if (deadline.aborted) throw Object.assign(new Error('Assistant request timed out'), { code: 'ECONNABORTED' })
    throw error
  }
}
export const sendAssistantMessage = (familyId, messages, signal, selection = {}) => post(familyId, 'chat', { messages, ...selection }, signal)
export const confirmAssistantProposal = (familyId, id, signal) => post(familyId, `proposals/${id}/confirm`, {}, signal)
export const cancelAssistantProposal = (familyId, id, signal) => post(familyId, `proposals/${id}/cancel`, {}, signal)
export function assistantErrorMessage(error) {
  const data = error.response?.data
  if (data?.errors?.length) return data.errors.join(' ')
  if (error.response?.status === 401) return 'Your session expired. Please log in again.'
  if (error.code === 'ERR_CANCELED') return 'Stopped waiting. If you were saving, check your tasks before preparing another proposal.'
  return data?.message || data?.error || (error.code === 'ECONNABORTED'
    ? 'The request timed out. If you were saving, check your tasks or retry the same confirmation.'
    : 'Unable to reach the assistant. Please try again.')
}

<script setup>
import { computed } from 'vue'

const props = defineProps({
  appearance: { type: Object, default: () => ({}) },
  showBackground: { type: Boolean, default: true }
})

const images = import.meta.glob('../../../assets/pets/**/*.png', {
  eager: true,
  query: '?url',
  import: 'default'
})
const findAsset = (path) => images[`../../../assets/pets/${path}`] || null
const species = computed(() => ['fox', 'cat'].includes(props.appearance?.species) ? props.appearance.species : 'fox')
const equipped = computed(() => props.appearance?.equipped || {})
const base = computed(() => findAsset(`${species.value}.png`))
const top = computed(() => equipped.value.outfit ? findAsset(`tops/${equipped.value.outfit}.png`) : null)
const bottom = computed(() => {
  const id = equipped.value.bottom || ''
  const folder = id.startsWith('skirts-') ? 'skirts' : id.startsWith('shorts-') ? 'shorts' : ''
  return folder ? findAsset(`${folder}/${id}.png`) : null
})
</script>

<template>
  <div class="pet-avatar" :class="{ 'pet-avatar--clear': !showBackground, 'pet-avatar--fox': species === 'fox' }" role="img" :aria-label="`${species} avatar with selected clothes`">
    <img v-if="base" class="pet-avatar__base" :src="base" alt="" draggable="false" />
    <img v-if="top" class="pet-avatar__part pet-avatar__top" :src="top" alt="" draggable="false" />
    <img v-if="bottom" class="pet-avatar__part pet-avatar__bottom" :src="bottom" alt="" draggable="false" />
  </div>
</template>

<style scoped>
.pet-avatar { position: relative; width: 100%; aspect-ratio: 1 / 1; overflow: hidden; border-radius: 26px; background: radial-gradient(circle at 50% 45%, var(--theme-panel, #fff) 0%, var(--theme-soft, #eaf7ed) 70%, var(--theme-danger-soft, #ffebed) 100%); isolation: isolate; }
.pet-avatar--clear { background: transparent; }
.pet-avatar img { display: block; position: absolute; object-fit: contain; pointer-events: none; user-select: none; }
.pet-avatar__base { width: 100%; height: 94%; left: 0; bottom: 0; }
.pet-avatar__part { filter: drop-shadow(0 2px 1px rgba(80,52,78,.1)); }
.pet-avatar__top { width: 78%; height: 39%; left: 11%; top: 39%; z-index: 2; }
.pet-avatar__bottom { width: 60%; height: 25%; left: 20%; top: 67%; z-index: 3; }
</style>

FILE: client/src/features/auth/services/authApi.js
================================================

import axios from 'axios'
import { queryClient } from '../../../services/queryClient.js'

const authApi = axios.create({
  baseURL: import.meta.env.VITE_API_URL,
  timeout: 10000,
  headers: {
    'Content-Type': 'application/json'
  }
})

export async function loginUser(email, password) {
  const response = await authApi.post('/auth/login', {
    email,
    password
  })

  return response.data
}

export function getLoginErrorMessage(error) {
  if (!error.response) {
    if (error.code === 'ECONNABORTED') {
      return 'The server is taking too long. Please try again.'
    }

    return 'Unable to connect to the server. Please check your connection.'
  }

  switch (error.response.status) {
    case 400:
      return error.response.data?.message || 'Please check your details.'

    case 401:
      return 'Incorrect email or password. Please try again.'

    case 429:
      return 'Too many login attempts. Please try again later.'

    case 500:
    case 502:
    case 503:
      return 'Something went wrong on our end. Please try again later.'

    default:
      return 'Unable to log in. Please try again.'
  }
}

export async function verifySession() {
  const token = sessionStorage.getItem('token')

  if (!token) {
    return { status: 'invalid' }
  }

  try {
    const response = await authApi.get('/auth/me', {
      headers: {
        Authorization: `Bearer ${token}`
      }
    })

    if (response.data.success === true && response.data.user) {
      // Refresh locally stored user details
      sessionStorage.setItem(
        'user',
        JSON.stringify(response.data.user)
      )

      return { status: 'valid' }
    }

    return { status: 'unavailable' }

  } catch (error) {
    // Token expired, revoked, malformed or user deleted
    if (error.response?.status === 401 ||
        error.response?.status === 404) {
      clearUserSession()
      return { status: 'invalid' }
    }

    // Network/server problems are not authentication failures
    return { status: 'unavailable' }
  }
}


export async function logoutUser() {
  const token = sessionStorage.getItem('token')

  if (!token) {
    return
  }

  await authApi.post(
    '/auth/logout',
    {},
    {
      headers: {
        Authorization: `Bearer ${token}`
      }
    }
  )
}

export function clearUserSession() {
  sessionStorage.removeItem('token')
  sessionStorage.removeItem('user')
  sessionStorage.removeItem('activeFamilyId')
  // Drop all cached family data so the next user never sees it
  queryClient.clear()
}


export async function getMyProfile() {
  const token = sessionStorage.getItem('token')

  const response = await authApi.get('/auth/me', {
    headers: {
      Authorization: `Bearer ${token}`
    }
  })

  return response.data.user
}

export async function getPublicProfile(userId) {
  const response = await authApi.get(`/auth/users/${encodeURIComponent(userId)}`, {
    headers: { Authorization: `Bearer ${sessionStorage.getItem('token')}` },
  })
  return response.data.user
}

export async function updateMyProfile(profile) {
  const token = sessionStorage.getItem('token')

  const response = await authApi.patch(
    '/auth/me',
    profile,
    {
      headers: {
        Authorization: `Bearer ${token}`
      }
    }
  )

  return response.data.user
}


export async function updateMyPet(appearance) {
  const token = sessionStorage.getItem('token')
  const response = await authApi.patch('/auth/me/pet', appearance, {
    headers: { Authorization: `Bearer ${token}` }
  })
  return response.data.user
}

FILE: client/src/features/auth/services/registerApi.js
================================================
import axios from 'axios'

const api = axios.create({
  baseURL: import.meta.env.VITE_API_URL,
  timeout: 15000,
  headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' }
})

export async function registerCaregiver(details) {
  const { data } = await api.post('/auth/register', details)
  if (data?.success !== true || !data.token || !data.user?.id) {
    throw new Error('Unexpected response from server. Please try logging in.')
  }
  return data
}

export function registrationErrorMessage(error) {
  if (error.response?.data?.message) return error.response.data.message
  if (error.code === 'ECONNABORTED') return 'The server is taking too long. Please try again.'
  if (!error.response) return 'Could not connect to CareCircle. Please check your connection.'
  return 'Account creation failed. Please try again.'
}

<script setup>
import { ref, computed } from 'vue'
import { useRouter } from 'vue-router'
import {
  joinFamily,
  getFamilyErrorMessage
} from '../../family/services/familyApi.js'
import { useActiveFamily } from '../../../composables/useActiveFamily.js'

import familyPoster from '../../../assets/create-family-hero.png'

const router = useRouter()
const { loadFamilies, selectFamily } = useActiveFamily()

const inviteCode = ref('')
const isLoading = ref(false)
const errorMessage = ref('')
const joinedFamily = ref(null)

const normalizedCode = computed(() =>
  inviteCode.value.trim().toUpperCase()
)

const isValid = computed(() =>
  /^[A-F0-9]{10}$/.test(normalizedCode.value) &&
  !isLoading.value
)

async function handleJoinFamily() {
  if (isLoading.value) return

  errorMessage.value = ''

  if (!isValid.value) {
    errorMessage.value =
      'Please enter a valid 10-character invitation code.'
    return
  }

  isLoading.value = true

  try {
    const response = await joinFamily(normalizedCode.value)

    if (response.success !== true || !response.family?.id) {
      throw new Error('Unexpected server response.')
    }

    joinedFamily.value = response.family

    // Remember newly joined family and refresh shared sidebar data
    selectFamily(response.family.id)
    await loadFamilies()

  } catch (error) {
    errorMessage.value = getFamilyErrorMessage(error)

  } finally {
    isLoading.value = false
  }
}

function goToFamily() {
  router.push('/home')
}
</script>

<script setup>
import { ref, computed } from 'vue'
import AuthShell from '../components/AuthShell.vue'
import { useRouter, useRoute } from 'vue-router'
import { loginUser, getLoginErrorMessage } from '../services/authApi.js'

const router = useRouter()
const route = useRoute()
const isLoading = ref(false)
const loginError = ref('')
const email = ref('')
const password = ref('')
const showPassword = ref(false)
const attempted = ref(false)
const emailValid = computed(() => /^[^\s@]+@[^\s@]+\.[^\s@]+$/.test(email.value.trim()))

async function handleLogin() {
  attempted.value = true
  loginError.value = ''

  // 1. Stop if email or password is invalid.
  if (!email.value.trim() || !password.value) {
    loginError.value = 'Please enter your email and password.'
    return
  }

  if (!/^[^\s@]+@[^\s@]+\.[^\s@]+$/.test(email.value.trim())) {
    loginError.value = 'Please enter a valid email address.'
    return
  }

  if (isLoading.value) return

  // 2. Set isLoading to true.
  isLoading.value = true

  try {
    // 3. Call loginUser(email.value, password.value).
    const response = await loginUser(email.value.trim(), password.value)

    // 4. Validate backend response.
    if (
      response.success !== true ||
      typeof response.token !== 'string' ||
      !response.token.trim() ||
      !response.user ||
      typeof response.user !== 'object' ||
      Array.isArray(response.user)
    ) {
      throw new Error('Invalid login response from server.')
    }

    // 5. Save authenticated session.
    // Replace this with your team's shared session handler.
    sessionStorage.setItem('token', response.token)
    sessionStorage.setItem('user', JSON.stringify(response.user))

    // 6. Navigate to family selection.
    await router.push('/home')

  } catch (error) {
    loginError.value = getLoginErrorMessage(error)
  } finally {
    // Always reset loading.
    isLoading.value = false
  }
}

</script>

<template>
  <AuthShell>
    <div class="auth-icon" aria-hidden="true">â™¥</div>
    <div class="auth-eyebrow">WELCOME BACK</div>
    <h2>Lovely to see you again!</h2>
    <p class="auth-subtitle">Log in to your family circle and keep the care going. â™¡</p>
    <p
      v-if="route.query.serviceUnavailable === '1'"
      class="auth-error"
      role="alert"
    >
      Unable to verify your session right now.
      Please try again when the server is available.
    </p>
    <form @submit.prevent="handleLogin" novalidate>
      <div class="form-group">
        <label for="email">Email address</label>
        <div class="input-wrap">
          <i class="bi bi-envelope" aria-hidden="true"></i><input id="email" v-model.trim="email" type="email"
            autocomplete="email" placeholder="you@example.com" :aria-invalid="attempted && !emailValid" />
        </div>
        <p v-if="attempted && !emailValid" class="field-error">Enter a valid email address.</p>
      </div>
      <div class="form-group">
        <div class="label-row">
          <label for="password">Password</label><span class="coming-soon">Forgot password? Â· Later</span>
        </div>
        <div class="input-wrap">
          <i class="bi bi-lock" aria-hidden="true"></i><input id="password" v-model="password"
            :type="showPassword ? 'text' : 'password'" autocomplete="current-password" placeholder="Enter your password"
            :aria-invalid="attempted && !password" /><button class="reveal" type="button"
            @click="showPassword = !showPassword" :aria-label="showPassword ? 'Hide password' : 'Show password'">
            <i :class="showPassword ? 'bi bi-eye-slash' : 'bi bi-eye'"></i>
          </button>
        </div>
        <p v-if="attempted && !password" class="field-error">Password is required.</p>
      </div>

        </template>

        <template v-else>

<script setup>
import { ref, computed, watch } from 'vue'
import { useRoute } from 'vue-router'
import { getPublicProfile } from '../services/authApi.js'
import CareAvatar from '../../../components/common/CareAvatar.vue'
import AvatarPreview from '../../avatar/components/AvatarPreview.vue'
import { defaultAppearance } from '../../avatar/data/avatarWardrobe.js'
import '../../../styles/profileView.css'

const route = useRoute()
const user = ref(null), loading = ref(false), error = ref('')
const languages = { en: 'English', zh: 'Chinese', ms: 'Malay', ta: 'Tamil' }
const taskStatuses = { claimed: 'Upcoming', in_progress: 'In progress', completed: 'Completed' }
function taskDate(task) {
  const date = task.status === 'completed' ? task.completedAt || task.startAt : task.startAt
  return date ? new Date(date).toLocaleDateString('en-SG', { day: 'numeric', month: 'short', year: 'numeric' }) : ''
}
const appearance = computed(() => ({
  baseId: user.value?.avatarAppearance?.baseId || defaultAppearance().baseId,
  equipped: { ...defaultAppearance().equipped, ...user.value?.avatarAppearance?.equipped },
}))
let request = 0
async function loadProfile() {
  const current = ++request
  loading.value = true; user.value = null; error.value = ''
  try {
    const profile = await getPublicProfile(route.params.userId)
    if (current === request) user.value = profile
  } catch (e) {
    if (current === request) error.value = e.response?.data?.message || 'Unable to load profile. Please try again.'
  } finally { if (current === request) loading.value = false }
}
watch(() => route.params.userId, loadProfile, { immediate: true })
</script>

<script setup>
import { computed, ref, watch } from 'vue'
import { findItem, categoryForBottom } from '../data/avatarWardrobe.js'

const props = defineProps({
  appearance: { type: Object, required: true }
})
const failed = ref({})
const layers = computed(() => {
  const a = props.appearance || {}
  const e = a.equipped || {}
  const bottomType = categoryForBottom(e.bottom)
  return [
    ['base', findItem('bases', a.baseId)],
    ...(e.dress
      ? [['dress', findItem('dresses', e.dress)]]
      : [
          ['bottom', bottomType ? findItem(bottomType, e.bottom) : null],
          ['top', findItem('tops', e.top)]
        ]),
    ['accessory', findItem('accessories', e.accessory)]
  ].filter(([, item]) => Boolean(item))
})
watch(layers, () => { failed.value = {} })
</script>

<template>
  <div class="cc-avatar" role="img" :aria-label="`${appearance.baseId || 'Pet'} wearing selected clothes`">
    <img
      v-for="([type, item], index) in layers"
      :key="`${type}-${item.id}`"
      v-show="!failed[item.id]"
      :src="item.image"
      :class="[
        'cc-avatar-layer',
        `cc-avatar-${type}`,
        type === 'bottom' ? (item.id.startsWith('skirts-') ? 'cc-avatar-skirt' : 'cc-avatar-shorts') : ''
      ]"
      :style="{ zIndex: index + 1 }"
      alt=""
      draggable="false"
      @error="failed[item.id] = true"
    />
    <div v-if="failed[appearance.baseId]" class="cc-avatar-warning">Character image missing</div>
  </div>
</template>

<style scoped>
.cc-avatar { position: relative; width: 100%; aspect-ratio: 1; isolation: isolate; }
.cc-avatar-layer { position: absolute; display: block; object-fit: contain; pointer-events: none; user-select: none; }
.cc-avatar-base { inset: 0; width: 100%; height: 100%; }
